verdict.charges: A Premier League independent commission found Manchester City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges against the club. One charge was not proven.
verdict.split: All 80 financial charges and 34 of the 35 failure-to-cooperate charges were proven. 80 + 34 = 114. One failure-to-cooperate charge was not proven.
verdict.groups: The 115 charges fall into five groups: 54 for inaccurate financial information, 14 for incomplete payments to players and managers, 7 under the Profitability and Sustainability Rules, 5 under UEFA financial rules, and 35 for failure to cooperate. 54 + 14 + 7 + 5 = 80.
verdict.dates: The verdict was reported on 25 September 2026 (Sky News video and Football Today). The Premier League confirmed it on Tuesday 29 September 2026 (CBS Sports, SportBible).
verdict.seasons: The financial charges cover the seasons 2009-10 to 2017-18, that is 2009 to 2018.
verdict.sham: The commission found sponsors paid less than their contracts stated and the owners made up the difference, which inflated revenue and cut costs by about 900 million pounds in total over those seasons: the club was more than 900 million pounds healthier on paper.
verdict.history: The charges were announced on 6 February 2023. The hearing ran about 10 weeks, from September to December 2024, before a three-person independent commission. The investigation began in 2018.

city_response.soriano: Ferran Soriano (SportBible, 13 November) said: The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation; that the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi.
city_response.club: City say they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence. Their lawyers say the commission's opinion contains clear, material errors of law, principle and fact and that it is unsafe. The club says it will be relentless.

appeal.lodged: City lodged an appeal on Thursday 1 October 2026 (deadline 2 October).
appeal.panel: The appeal goes to a new three-person panel.
appeal.hearing: The hearing is expected in the middle of December 2026 and could last several days: at most 5 days, concluding within 12 weeks, with a verdict within 30 days. The appeal judgment is expected in the new year. SportBible on 27 November, quoting analyst Stefan Borson, says the appeal likely begins on 12 December and lasts 5 to 10 days.

sanctions.undecided: Sanctions have not been decided. If the appeal fails, the options run from fines and points deductions up to expulsion from the league.
sanctions.timing: Sanctions are expected early next year. Punishments can themselves be appealed, so the uncertainty could run beyond the end of the season in May, and could continue for years (reports mention 2028 or 2029).
sanctions.panel: A sanctions hearing would be by the same three-person panel as the 2024 hearing (Sky Sports, 12 October).

clubs.view: SportBible on 27 November, citing BBC Sport: executives at three Premier League clubs believe City's owners should be forced to sell the club should the appeal fail. 18 of the 20 clubs voted to cover legal costs for board directors; only Nottingham Forest and City voted against.

league.table: Wikipedia's 2026-27 Premier League table as of 27 November: Arsenal 1st with 28 points from 11 games; Manchester City 3rd with 22 points from 11 games, 7 wins, 1 draw and 3 defeats, 22 goals for and 14 against. Arsenal lead City by 6 points.
league.manager: Enzo Maresca was appointed on 29 June 2026, succeeding Pep Guardiola (Wikipedia, 2026-27 Manchester City season).
league.results: City lost 3-1 at Nottingham Forest, drew 1-1 with Fulham and drew 2-2 with Napoli in the Champions League. City's next opponent is Arsenal (club's own Manager's Preview video, 27 November).
